minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  January 11, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
January 11, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Morales; and
  Absent:  Council Members Padilla, and Faulk.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Items
No. CS-1 and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:02 p.m.

The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member Faulk.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/ Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.

There was no response.

  1
   January 11, 2022

101  RESOLUTION NO. 22-37 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO
  IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE PUBLIC MEETINGS FROM JANUARY 11,
  2022, THROUGH FEBRUARY 10, 2022 PER ASSEMBLY BILL 361. Staff report
  dated January 11, 2022, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  authorizing the City to implement teleconference public meetings from January 11, 2022,
  through February 10, 2022, for the City Council and all other legislative bodies, pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that Resolution No. 22-37 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND ALL OTHER
  LEGISLATIVE BODIES TO CONTINUE TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM JANUARY 11, 2022,
  THROUGH FEBRUARY 10, 2022, PUSUANT TO AB 361

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

  Mayor Butts read a Public Notice from the City of Inglewood Housing Protection
  Department, canceling all scheduled residential registry workshops because of the
  increase in COVID-19. Mayor Butts stated that this cancellation is a precaution taken in
  the interest of public health and safety.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  January 6, 2022, in the amount of $4,349,824.80 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Faulk.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on November 23, 2021,
  November 24, 2021 (Special), and November 30, 2021, be approved. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Lilia Giron for alleged personal injuries; sidewalk condition on August 12, 2021.
  2. Robin Danztler, Samuel Small, Samantha Small, and Robert Small for alleged
  wrongful death on June 19, 2021.
  3. John Weaver for alleged property damage; fire hydrant malfunction on September 7,
  2021.
  B. Reject Insufficient Claim Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1. Donald Penn for alleged tire damage; road condition on October 24, 2021.

  2
   January 11, 2022

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-3; and 2) Reject
  Claim listed as B-1. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 22-38 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-
  2022 ANNUAL BUDGET TO FURNISH AND INSTALL NEW HEATING,
  VENTILATION, AND AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEMS AT EDWARD
  VINCENT PARK’S WILLIE AGEE PLAYHOUSE; CONTRACT AWARDED
  AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-103 APPROVED – TRI-CHEM TECHNOLOGY
  CORPORATION. Staff report dated January 11, 2022, was presented recommending
  award of contract and approval of an agreement with Tri-Chem Technology Corporation
  to furnish and install new Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) System at
  Willie Agee Playhouse in Edward Vincent Jr., Park, per Bid No. RFB-0140.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 22-38 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  AMENDING THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL BUDGET TO FURNISH AND
  INSTALL  NEW  HEATING,  VENTILATION  AND  AIR
  CONDITIONING SYSTEMS AT EDWARD VINCENT PARK’S
  WILLIE AGEE PLAYHOUSE

  and 2) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 22-103 in the total amount of
  $104,390 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in an amount not to exceed $9,490).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

301  ORDINANCE NO 22-04 ADOPTED – DESIGNATING CERTAIN PORTIONS OF
  THE CITY AS AN “EVENT ZONE” TO REGULATE CERTAIN ACTIVITIES IN
  CONNECTION WITH SUPER BOWL LVI AND RELATED EVENTS. Staff report
  dated January 11, 2022, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 22-04
  to designate certain portions of the City as an “Event Zone” in order to regulate certain
  activities in connection with Super Bowl LVI and related events.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 22-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  DESIGNATING CERTAIN PORTIONS OF THE CITY AS AN “EVENT
  ZONE” IN ORDER TO REGULATE CERTAIN ACTIVITIES IN
  CONNECTION WITH SUPER BOWL LVI AND RELATED EVENTS

  which was introduced at the meeting held January 4, 2022, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Faulk.

  3
   January 11, 2022

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY/CLIENT PRIVILEGED;
  FARMERS INSURANCE EXCHANGE (ASO – CATHY GILL). Closed Session –
  Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d) (2) pertaining to significant exposure to
  litigation pertaining Claim dated August 9, 2021; Farmers Insurance Exchange (ASO-
  Cathy Gill), Claim No.: 21-15720.

  Absent: Council Members Padilla, and Faulk.

  Discussion was held; Direction given to staff.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY/CLIENT PRIVILEGED;
  LEONARD WAYNE WILLIAMS, JR. V. ALLTECH PROTECTIVE SERVICES,
  ET AL.:  LASC CASE NO. BC717771.  Closed Session – Confidential –
  Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding
  Pending Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Leonard Wayne
  Williams, Jr. v. Alltech Protective Services, et al.: LASC Case No: BC717771.

  Absent: Council Members Padilla, and Faulk.

  Discussion was held; Direction given to staff.

101  REPORTS – CITY MANANGER. Acting City Manager Louis Atwell reported on the
  Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day Celebration cancellation. He also reported that the city
  planned to acknowledge and celebrate the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day speech contest
  winners. He stated Inglewood students from schools and churches would write and present
  their speeches, with the winners being chosen on Monday, January 17, 2022. Additionally,
  he thanked the Rams Organization for providing cash prizes for the four winners out of 40
  who competed. Finally, he reported staff was working with the Rams Organization to
  determine a safe venue to celebrate the winners.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, congratulated her
  staff Angela Allen and Kailyn Austin on their one year of service in the City Clerk’s
  Office. She also thanked them for their dedicated work and commitment to the City of
  Inglewood. She wished herself and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. a Happy Birthday.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Henry Hank Harris, long term resident of District 2, Enrique
  Borrel, Truro Block Club Member, and Gil Mathieu at the hour of 2:15 p.m.

  Approved this 8th day of February, 2022.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
